finding: 019c31e rewrote §1 to read "One deliverable, and it is behaviour-preserving by default ... changes nothing for a project that does not set it" and, in the same commit, rewrote Non-Goal 6 to read "The breakdown is in scope and ships on --merge" — a new by_severity key emitted by tp audit --merge for every project, whether or not audit_converge_on is set. That is a second deliverable and it is not behaviour-preserving by default, which is the exact sentence shape §1 had just been repaired for removing ("§3 changes consecutive_clean and converged for any project whose spec moves between rounds, opted in or not"). The repair fixed the paragraph and reintroduced the condition that made it wrong.
suggestion: Pick one. Either keep the release single-deliverable and return the --merge by_severity breakdown to spec/0.46.0.md §8.3 (which already says the breakdown is 0.37.0's, so both files move together), or restate §1 as "two deliverables: audit_converge_on, which is opt-in, and a by_severity breakdown on tp audit --merge, which is unconditional" and drop the "changes nothing" clause.

finding: Non-Goal 6 puts a by_severity breakdown on tp audit --merge in scope, but nothing else in the file carries it. §5 lists eleven tests and none exercises --merge; §5's preamble says "Every test names the input that makes it fail", and §5's closing paragraph — "What is not tested here, named so its absence is deliberate" — names only role_streaks[].open and spec_coverage_clean_rounds, so the breakdown is neither tested nor listed as deliberately untested. §2's cost paragraph enumerates the surfaces the twin touches (tp config --extract, tp validate --project) and does not mention --merge either. The --compact disposition of the new key is also unstated, although the same sentence notes :90-92 already carries a --compact-stripped key, and skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:641 is where every key's --compact disposition is recorded.
suggestion: Add a §5 test for the --merge breakdown naming its failing input (a merged round with one error, one warning and one info non-PASS row must emit by_severity {error:1,warning:1,info:1}, and PASS rows must not be counted), state whether by_severity survives --compact, and add --merge to §2's surface list.

finding: 019c31e added "`spec/0.31.0.md:41` and `spec/0.35.0.md:568-573` keep their copies: those are shipped specs and `spec/0.34.0.md` Non-Goal 6 forbids editing one." The 0.35.0 half is false and the paragraph contradicts itself two sentences later. Read: spec/0.35.0.md:568-573 is the CORRECTED three-layer statement ("which for workflow fields is task override > project config > built-in ... Two exceptions: notify_cmd ... and TP_RUNNER_SEAM"). The five-layer copy in that file is at :575 alone, and only as a record of an earlier draft. The next sentence of §2 then calls the same range "the most accurate text in the repository on this point" — so one paragraph says :568-573 both carries the error Non-Goal 6 forbids fixing and is the most accurate text there is. Round 5's own commit a6d80f1 got this right in its message: "spec/0.35.0.md:575 keeps its copy: that one is the historical record of the removal." The repair replaced a correct pointer with a wrong one.
suggestion: Cite spec/0.35.0.md:575, not :568-573, as the surviving copy — and say it is the historical record of the removal rather than an uncorrected error, since Non-Goal 6 is not why it stands. Keep the separate reference to §7/:568-573 as the accurate statement.

finding: Non-Goal 6 now reads "... The review side emits `nonblocking_open` (`review_record.go:231`) Four places pin its absence on `--record`/`--status` by name, counted: ...". The rewrite dropped the conjunction the old text had ("and **four** places pin") and left two sentences fused with no punctuation. It is the one item in the file a reader must parse to know what is deferred versus in scope, and this is the third round in which Non-Goal 6 has been rewritten.
suggestion: Close the sentence after (`review_record.go:231`) and begin the next with "Four places pin its absence on --record/--status by name, counted:".

finding: cdcc3cc added a provenance note to spec/0.46.0.md §8.4: "§2–§8.3 come from v0.36.0's audit; this comes from v0.37.0's review." The boundary is drawn in the wrong place and the repair therefore introduced a fresh false claim while fixing an unstated one. §8.1, §8.2 and §8.3 were written in commit 43f29e8 (2026-09-02 01:11), thirty-four minutes before cdcc3cc, and that commit's own message says why: "Measured in round 4: spec/0.46.0.md contained zero occurrences of severity, wontfix, disposition, --resolve or dedupAuditRows" — i.e. they came from v0.37.0's review, exactly like §8.4. The bodies say so too: §8.2 reads "both were withdrawn within a round, which is why it is here rather than there", and §8.3 reads "spec/0.37.0.md §2 said so on the same day". §8a is a third counterexample: it was added in 82d8ee9, also 2026-09-02, from field feedback measured in two other repositories, and the note's "§2–§8.3" range silently excludes it while §1 still claims every section is v0.36.0 audit output.
suggestion: State the boundary over what was actually counted: §2–§8 come from v0.36.0's audit; §8.1–§8.4 come from v0.37.0's review; §8a comes from field feedback in two other repositories. Move the note out of §8.4 to the file header or §1, since it now qualifies §1's claim rather than one subsection's.

finding: The file header records the rewrite decision this file was rebuilt on: the withdrawn-draft prose "had grown to 77 of the file's 306 lines, which is spec/0.43.0.md §2's repair-verbosity class measured on this file." Three rounds of repairs have undone it. snapshot-round-6.md is 265 lines; spec/0.37.0.md is now 311 — larger than the 306 the header names as the problem — and 019c31e alone added 46 lines (+78/-32) and 506 words, almost all of it new draft retrospective: "An earlier draft of this section wrote the five-layer chain", "This paragraph described the two-deliverable release for one round after the cut", "an earlier draft counted six and the count was copied into spec/0.46.0.md before anyone checked it", "it is narrower than an earlier draft claimed", "an earlier draft scoped the docs by file". A fixed 12-phrase probe for that prose shape counts 17 hits in snapshot-round-6.md and 20 in the current file. Each of these is text the next round must read and can find a defect in, which is the mechanism §3 of spec/0.43.0.md describes.
suggestion: Apply the header's own rule to the repairs it now covers: keep the corrected statement, delete the account of the draft it replaced, and keep the retrospective only where a reader would otherwise re-propose the removed thing (§1's pointer to §3, and §3 itself). Deleting the five 'an earlier draft' clauses named above costs no decision and returns the file to roughly its post-rewrite size.

finding: Two CLAUDE.md pointers into spec/0.37.0.md still name sections that exist but no longer hold what is claimed, and both survived round 5's sweep. Measured against git: at 907b8df the file's headings were 1 Overview, 2 audit_converge_on, 3 A disposition that says accepted stops blocking, 4 A changed spec ends the streak, 5 The gate tp reports and the gate this project ships on are not the same gate, 6 Non-Goals, 7 Tests; at HEAD they are 1 Overview, 2 audit_converge_on, 3 What this release deliberately does not contain, 4 Non-Goals, 5 Tests. So (a) CLAUDE.md:206 "spec/0.37.0.md §5 takes the divergence" now points at the test list — the divergence is §4 Non-Goal 1 and spec/0.46.0.md §8 — and commit 975a1b8, whose subject is "correct the precedence chain at its source, and two stale 0.37.0 pointers", rewrote the second half of that same sentence and left the pointer; (b) CLAUDE.md:259 "0.41.0 is the durability half of 0.37.0 §3" points at the cut record, and spec/0.41.0.md:6-8 already declares that dependency void. Commit a014e14 asserts "Repo-wide sweep over every spec, CLAUDE.md, README.md and both skill files now returns zero broken file or section references" — true only of a sweep that checks existence, which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md:264-268 already names.
suggestion: Repoint CLAUDE.md:206 at spec/0.46.0.md §8 (or spec/0.37.0.md §4 Non-Goal 1) and CLAUDE.md:259 at spec/0.46.0.md §8.1, matching spec/0.41.0.md's own header. Then treat the sweep as unfinished: an existence check cannot settle a renumber, so re-read each surviving reference for whether the section still means what the sentence says.

finding: CLAUDE.md's roadmap table carries a Lines column that this batch invalidated for the two files it touched, and CLAUDE.md:230-236 makes that column load-bearing — it is the measured predictor the thirteen-release split was decided on. Counted at HEAD: spec/0.37.0.md is 311 lines against the table's 265 (019c31e added 46), and spec/0.46.0.md is 482 against the table's 253 (cdcc3cc added 26 on top of an already stale figure). Two other rows are stale from earlier work: 0.49.0 is 561 against 501 and 0.41.0 is 72 against 63.
suggestion: Refresh the column, or replace the numbers with the command that derives them (wc -l spec/*.md), since CLAUDE.md's own rule is that a claim bound to a named artifact cannot rot silently while a measured constant in prose goes stale faster than a release.

finding: 8dc02b5 replaced the pluginMinVersion constant with a helper that reads .claude-plugin/plugin.json, which is right for the four call sites in hooks_session_start_test.go but turned one assertion into a tautology. TestPluginManifestDeclaresIdentity:92 now reads assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, comparePluginVersions(t, manifest.Version, pluginMinVersion(t)), 0): manifest.Version comes from readRepoDoc(t, pluginManifestPath) and pluginMinVersion(t) reads filepath.Join(repoRoot(t), pluginManifestPath) — the same field of the same file, so comparePluginVersions always returns 0 and the assertion cannot fail for any manifest content. The rewritten message admits it in words: "plugin.json's version is the preflight minimum, so it may not fall below itself". Before the change the same line compared the manifest against an independent literal and could fail. The commit message reports verifying the helper is discriminating by pointing it at a missing manifest — that mutation kills the require.NoError inside the helper, not this assertion, so the check that was run does not cover the line that lost its arm. Coverage is not zero (TestPluginVersionIsNotBehindTheLatestTag still catches a downgrade below the newest tag) but :92 itself is now dead, in a repo whose CLAUDE.md names the tautological assertion as the thing to watch for.
suggestion: Delete lines 92-93 and let TestPluginVersionIsNotBehindTheLatestTag carry the ordering claim, or give the assertion an independent second operand (the newest git tag, or the version the session-start hook parses out of the manifest with its own sed expression, which would additionally pin that the shell parser and the Go parser agree).

finding: Bumping the manifest to 0.37.0 during review round 6 sets the SessionStart preflight's minimum to a version that has no released binary, and the effect is live rather than theoretical. Measured: /tmp/tp-dev/tp built from this tree reports v0.36.1-0.20260901224505-8dc02b58bd44+dirty, and running hooks/session-start.sh against it exits 2 with "tp v0.36.1-... is older than the tp plugin's minimum 0.37.0", so tp resume --compact is no longer injected into any Claude Code session in this repository for the rest of the cycle — the plugin's own orientation, during the cycle that dogfoods it. The remedy the hook prints cannot fix it: go install ...@latest resolves to v0.36.0. hooks/session-start.sh:44-49 documents refusing the pre-tag window as correct, so this is not the hook misbehaving; what changed is the window's length. CLAUDE.md:164's rule is "bump → commit → tag (the >= comparison exists so that window is legal)", which assumes a window measured in one commit, and marketplace.json's source is "./", so anyone who runs claude plugin update tp@tp before the tag gets a manifest demanding a binary that does not exist.
suggestion: Either move the bump back to immediately before the tag and let TestPluginVersionIsBumpedWhenPluginContentChanges hold against the version at the last tag rather than forcing a bump mid-cycle, or state explicitly in CLAUDE.md:164 that a mid-cycle bump disables the plugin's orientation for the remainder of the cycle and that the hook's install hint is unfollowable in that window.

finding: 8dc02b5 also re-encoded the author name in the manifest, from "Yunus Emre Deligöz" to "Yunus Emre Delig\u00f6z", which its commit message does not mention — the message is about deriving the preflight minimum and bumping the version. It parses to the same string, so nothing breaks, but .claude-plugin/marketplace.json:6 still carries the literal ö, so two hand-maintained files in the same directory now disagree on encoding, and the next hand edit will silently flip it back and show up as a diff nobody intended.
suggestion: Restore the literal ö so the manifest matches marketplace.json, and if a tool re-serialized the file, name the tool in the commit message so the next reader does not read the escape as deliberate.

finding: I nearly filed §2's "that sweep is done rather than owed" as false. My injected copy of CLAUDE.md still showed the Deferred Ideas bullet reading "effective values resolve at read time (CLI > env > task override > project config > built-in)", which would have made the demotion of that sentence from scope to provenance a repair that dropped a live uncorrected carrier — the strongest finding of the round, if true. Reading the file instead of the injected copy killed it: CLAUDE.md:327-332 was corrected in a6d80f1 and now reads task override > project config > built-in with the reason attached, skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:521-529 splits the chain by field kind, and a literal search for "CLI > env" across the tree returns exactly two hits, both in shipped specs (spec/0.31.0.md:41, spec/0.35.0.md:575) that Non-Goal 6 protects. The sweep claim holds. Recording it because the failure mode is general: an agent's injected context is a snapshot of the repository at session start, and in a cycle where the repository is being repaired between rounds it is stale by construction — any finding derived from it must be re-derived against the file.
suggestion: No change to the spec. If it is worth mechanizing, a search for "CLI > env" outside spec/ is a one-line workflow.checks entry whose subject already exists in the review phase.
